controls.title: Protection of records
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That records held outside the chain (filesystem, primary databases) are protected. The chain protects records from the point of inclusion forward.
controls.what_we_prove: Records submitted to the chain are stored with tamper-evident ordering and cryptographic anchoring. They cannot be modified, deleted, or falsified without mathematically detectable evidence.

controls.title: Logging
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the logging was correctly configured to capture relevant events, that retention duration was appropriate, or that the log content was complete.
controls.what_we_prove: Logs submitted to the chain are stored with tamper-evident ordering, signed timestamps, and cryptographic anchoring. An auditor can verify the recorded logs are exactly as emitted.

controls.title: Monitoring activities
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That monitoring coverage was adequate, that the right behaviors were monitored, or that responses to anomalies were timely.
controls.what_we_prove: Monitoring-activity events submitted to the chain are recorded with stable cryptographic ordering and signed timestamps. An auditor can reconstruct the exact monitoring sequence.

controls.title: Clock synchronisation
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That client-side timestamps embedded in event payloads accurately reflect wall-clock time at the emitter. The chain attests the time of inclusion, not the time of the underlying action.
controls.what_we_prove: Events submitted to the chain carry server-attested timestamps from synchronized clocks. The relative ordering of events is mathematically stable.

controls_out_of_scope.reason: organizational controls (policies, roles, contacts, intelligence, etc.) are document- and process-level
privacy and protection of PII is policy-level
independent review, compliance, and documented operating procedures are procedural
people controls (screening, terms, awareness, disciplinary, NDAs, remote working, reporting) are HR-level
physical controls (perimeters, entry, supplies, working areas, equipment, etc.) are physical
user endpoint, access rights, source-code access, capacity, etc. are system-configuration; specific access events may be logged

vulnerability management, change management, capacity, malware protection, masking, leakage prevention, backup, redundancy, network controls, services, segregation, web filtering, cryptography, secure development, etc. are operational design
